To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transition metal coordination polymers of trans-1, 4-cyclo hexanedicarboxylic acid can be synthesized in aqueous solutions by a simple and convenient procedure.

(a) a careful control of pH and reaction conditions can be used to direct the crystallisation of a particular metal chdc2− coordination polymer, and (b) the magnetic properties of these compounds can be tuned by changing the metal centre and the dimensionality of the framework structure

(i) five new metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) were synthesized, characterized and investigated; (ii) the compounds 1,4,5 possess interesting magnetic properties, (iii) the compounds 4 and 1 were further investigated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis and characterization of five new coordination polymers based on the 1,4-cyclododecanedicarboxylato ligand and transition metals (M = Co, Fe, Cd, Mn), and their magnetic, thermal and structural properties.
the design of new metal–organic coordination polymers with the chdc2− ligand.

the development of the new metal-organic frameworks based on the trans-1, 4-cyclo-hexanedicarboxylic acid, which are synthesized in aqueous media and possess different structures and physical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of the compounds 1–5 was directed by pH, reaction temperature, and solvent composition.
the synthesis of the compounds is highly pH-sensitive.
the pH of reaction medium, temperature and solvent composition are the key factors in controlling the crystallization of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transition metal chdc2− coordination polymers can be synthesized in a wide range of pH and temperature conditions, and that the obtained compounds can be characterized by different structures, magnetic and thermal properties.
a careful control of the reaction conditions is essential for obtaining a desired product and the resulting compounds can be further utilized for various purposes.
the compounds of this study could serve as promising candidates for applications in gas storage, magnetism, heterogeneous catalysis and drug delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH of the solution can be used to control the formation of the different compounds.
by controlling pH, reaction temperature, solvent composition and metal ion type, a variety of MOF structures may be obtained.
it is possible to synthesize a variety of coordination polymers with a common building unit, trans-1, 4-cyclo-hexanedicarboxylic acid, by simply controlling the reaction conditions.
